# Prompt - LangChain4J and Gemini API

This example illustrates how to prompt [Gemini](https://gemini.google.com/)
using its client API. It performs a single prompt interaction and does not
initiate a conversational exchange with the model.

The implementation uses
[LangChain4J](https://github.com/langchain4j/langchain4j), a Java-based
framework for developing applications powered by large language models (LLMs),
similar to [LangChain for Python](https://www.langchain.com/). LangChain4J
provides tools for prompt management, LLM call chaining, memory handling,
retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and integration with external data
sources—all within the Java ecosystem.

[Spring AI](https://spring.io/projects/spring-ai) is another framework that
offers an abstraction layer between LLMs and the application.

This example connects to Google’s Gemini AI, hosted on Google Cloud. An API
key—available from [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey)—is
required. At the time of writing, Google provides a generous free tier, which is
more than sufficient for this use case.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

- [Google AI Studio API Key](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey)

- [`jq`](https://jqlang.org/)

## Run the example

1. Google AI Studio API Key

   If you have not already done so, please create an API key from
   [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey). This example searches
   for the key in the following order:

    1. System property: `gemini.api.key`
       (e.g. `java -Dgemini.api.key=[API-KEY] ...`)
    2. Environment variable: `GEMINI_API_KEY`
       (e.g. `GEMINI_API_KEY=[API-KEY] java ...`)
    3. File: `~/.gemini/api.key`

   For security purposes and to prevent exposing the API key in documentation,
   the following commands assume the key is saved in the `.gemini/api.key` file
   within the user’s home directory.

   Verify that the Cohere APIs can be successfully invoked. The following
   command assumes that the API key is stored at `~/.cohere/api.key`.

   ```shell
   curl 'https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-3-flash-preview:generateContent' \
     --silent \
     --request POST \
     --header "x-goog-api-key: $(cat ~/.gemini/api.key)" \
     --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     --data '{
     "contents": [
       {
         "parts": [
           {
             "text": "When did humans first land on the Moon?"
           }
         ]
       }
     ]
   }' | jq
   ```

   The model response

   ```json
   {
     "candidates": [
       {
         "content": {
           "parts": [
             {
               "text": "Humans first landed on the Moon on **July 20, 1969**.\n\nThe landing was part of NASA’s **Apollo 11** mission. **Neil Armstrong** and **Buzz Aldrin** landed the Lunar Module *Eagle* at 20:17 UTC. A few hours later, Neil Armstrong became the first human to step onto the lunar surface, famously declaring, \"That's one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind.\"\n\nWhile Armstrong and Aldrin explored the surface, the third crew member, **Michael Collins**, remained in lunar orbit aboard the Command Module *Columbia*.",
               "thoughtSignature": ""
             }
           ],
           "role": "model"
         },
         "finishReason": "STOP",
         "index": 0
       }
     ],
     "usageMetadata": {
       "promptTokenCount": 9,
       "candidatesTokenCount": 132,
       "totalTokenCount": 417,
       "promptTokensDetails": [
         {
           "modality": "TEXT",
           "tokenCount": 9
         }
       ],
       "thoughtsTokenCount": 276
     },
     "modelVersion": "gemini-3-flash-preview",
     "responseId": "Mhr4afy8GsiajrEP_t-Q6QE"
   }
   ```

2. Build the application

   This step assumes that a valid Google AI Studio API key is available at
   `~/.gemini/api.key`. See Step 1 for more information about how to do this.

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean verify
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the application was created and the dependencies
   copied.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './target/libs'
   ```

   The application JAR file and its dependencies.

   ```
   ./target/libs
   ├── jackson-annotations-2.21.jar
   ├── jackson-core-2.21.1.jar
   ├── jackson-databind-2.21.1.jar
   ├── jspecify-1.0.0.jar
   ├── langchain4j-1.14.0.jar
   ├── langchain4j-core-1.14.0.jar
   ├── langchain4j-google-ai-gemini-1.14.0.jar
   ├── langchain4j-http-client-1.14.0.jar
   ├── langchain4j-http-client-jdk-1.14.0.jar
   ├── logback-classic-1.5.32.jar
   ├── logback-core-1.5.32.jar
   ├── opennlp-tools-2.5.4.jar
   ├── prompt-langchain4j-gemini-api-1.0.0.jar
   └── slf4j-api-2.0.17.jar

   1 directory, 14 files
   ```

3. Run the program

   This step assumes that a valid Google AI Studio API key is available at
   `~/.gemini/api.key`. See Step 1 for more information about how to do this.

   Run the example with the default prompt.

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/*' \
     demo.Main
   ```

   Although the prompt remains the same, the output may vary with each run.

   ```
   prompt> When did humans first land on the Moon?
   assistant> Humans first landed on the Moon on **July 20, 1969**.

   This was accomplished by the United States' Apollo 11 mission, with astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin being the first two people to walk on the lunar surface.
   ```

   Run the example again with specific prompt.

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/*' \
     demo.Main 'Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?'
   ```

   The model should respond with 'Neil Armstrong', as he was the first person to
   walk on the Moon.

   ```
   prompt> Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
   assistant> The first person to walk on the Moon was **Neil Armstrong**.

   He stepped onto the lunar surface on **July 20, 1969**, during the Apollo 11 mission. His famous words were, "That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind."
   ```
